description: Compute the monthly payment on a balloon loan and the lump-sum balloon balance still due at the end of the term.

faqs.a: You make regular amortized payments for a fixed period (e.g. 7 years), then owe the entire remaining balance as one lump sum. The payment is calculated as if the loan amortized over a longer period.
The remaining balance after the balloon period is B = P(1+r)^k − M·(((1+r)^k − 1)/r), where k is the number of payments made.
faqs.q: How is the balloon balance calculated?

faqs.a: Balloon loans carry refinancing risk: if you cannot refinance or pay the lump sum when it comes due, you may face default. Plan for it early.
faqs.q: What are the risks of a balloon payment?

howto: Enter the loan amount, rate and full amortization period.
Enter when the balloon payment is due (in years).
Read the monthly payment and the lump sum you will owe at that point.
